I've just expanded our media production studio's internal server rack and need our hardware inventory properly tracked for insurance purposes. Here's what happened:

1. We purchased three new pieces of hardware last month (2024-11-15):
   - A Dell PowerEdge R740 server (brand: Dell, model: PowerEdge R740) — cost us $1,850.00, draws about 110 watts, 36-month warranty, located in 'Rack U2', serial DEL-R740-001, notes: 'Primary production VM host'
   - A Cisco SG300-28 switch (brand: Cisco, model: SG300-28) — cost $320.00, draws 32 watts, 36-month warranty, located in 'Rack U8', serial CSC-SG300-001
   - An APC Smart-UPS 1500 (brand: APC, model: SMT1500) — cost $480.00, draws 60 watts, 24-month warranty, located in 'Rack U10', serial APC-SMT-001, notes: 'Protects rack gear'

2. We had an old 4TB Seagate NAS drive (just add it with the name 'Seagate NAS 4TB HDD', type drive, purchase date 2020-03-01, price $89.00, 24-month warranty, location 'Storage Shelf', serial SGT-4TB-001) that has now failed and been pulled from service — mark it appropriately in the system.

3. The Cisco SG300-28 we just added is actually going to be relocated — update its location to 'Storage Closet' and add a note 'Spare switch, replaced by SG550'.

4. Finally, generate an insurance-ready asset report saved to a file called 'homelab_insurance_report.md' in the workspace. Our local electricity rate is $0.18 per kWh — make sure the power cost estimate reflects this exact rate.
